experiment: pinned Ibex Simple System timing audit for RTNN input-indexed LUT loads
interpretation: For the exact RTL-tested RTNN binary and pinned one-host Ibex Simple System, all neural-input-indexed memory loads are aligned LW instructions into two finite LUTs wholly resident in the 1 MiB on-chip simulation RAM. All 12,290 legal LUT word addresses uniquely decode to that RAM. The synthesized ram_2p response-valid control is a single async-reset FF whose D input is exactly the request and whose transitive fan-in contains no address signal. Together with the pinned bus response-selection structure, the LUT address may change the returned value but not the one-cycle response latency in this memory model.
negative_or_discarded_controls: An earlier sequential SAT harness using async2sync with an unconstrained clock was discarded as an unsuitable model; its counterexample was not interpreted as a RAM timing failure.

BINSEC generic relational memory analysis for class 1 previously hit runner resource limits; the present result is target-specific to deterministic address-independent Simple System RAM rather than a generic memory constant-time theorem.
nonclaims: No constant-latency claim is transferred to caches, external SDRAM, arbitration fabrics, or DE0-CV memory.
Data values are address-dependent; only response timing is address-independent under this pinned RAM/bus model.
This is not an FPGA/ASIC/silicon WCET certificate.
A different bus map, number of hosts, memory RTL, compiler artifact, or target integration requires new evidence.
